title: Muse Spark Open on DGX Spark: NVFP4 to mixed 2-bit (IQ2_XXS and Q2_K) requantization, the seeded expert cache and prefill batch sizing
purpose: Starting from stock llama.cpp and the official Muse Spark Open NVFP4 checkpoint, how much do time to first token, decode rate and total request time change when the routed experts are requantized to a mixed 2-bit format (IQ2_XXS for the gate and up projections, Q2_K for down), again when the profile-seeded expert cache is added, and again when the prefill batch is sized so each prompt streams the experts once?

covers: client time to first token, decode tokens per second and total request time at 512 and 2048 rendered prompt tokens, cold and warm
the NVFP4 GGUF pack built from the official checkpoint, and a mixed 2-bit requantization of it (IQ2_XXS for the gate and up projections, Q2_K for down)
greedy output parity with the cache gate unset, and the activation marker with it set
the server prefill batch size chosen by the prefill batch sizing capsule
paired MMLU accuracy of the 2-bit pack against the NVFP4 pack: non-inferiority within 5 points
excludes: accuracy beyond the paired MMLU zero-shot gate (generation quality, reasoning, long contexts)
hardware other than one DGX Spark

client_ttft_ms.how: Client clock from sending the request to the first streamed token.

decode_tokens_per_second.how: Generated tokens after the first, over the time they took, from the server's timings.

request_total_ms.how: Client clock from sending the request to the last streamed token (32 generated tokens).

prompt_tokens_per_second.how: Prompt tokens over prompt processing time, from the server's timings.

sampled_peak_memory_bytes.how: Highest sampled resident memory of the engine process group under the cap.

load_seconds.how: From engine start to the health endpoint answering ready.

protocol.notes: One server load per arm (A, B, C, D in that order). Per prompt size: one cold request (pack pages evicted with posix_fadvise DONTNEED before it, reported separately) then one warm request, 32 generated tokens each. Trimmed to keep the lab short: with a single warm request there is no warm spread, so small differences are reported as measured, not as gains.

checks.does: The server's prompt token count equals the request's rendered prompt token count.
On E1 with the cache gate unset, greedy output of each request equals arm B byte for byte.
With the cache gate set, the engine prints expert_weight_cache: active.
E0 on a pack without expert .scale tensors gives the same greedy output as stock.
An expert matmul and a layer slice of the NVFP4 pack match a torch dequantization of the checkpoint within tolerance.
Every routed expert weight of the NVFP4 pack is NVFP4 with its .scale tensor.
Every routed gate and up expert weight of the 2-bit pack is IQ2_XXS and every down expert weight Q2_K; other tensors keep their NVFP4-pack type.

The arm D server prints the planned n_batch and n_ubatch, its device buffers fit the plan budget, and its greedy outputs agree with arm C (byte-identical or a common prefix of at least 64 characters, since a different micro-batch split changes the float summation order).
Paired MMLU zero-shot accuracy of the 2-bit pack against the NVFP4 pack on E0: at the first decisive planned checkpoint the upper bound of the loss is below 5 points (eval.paired_accuracy).
One cold request under the memory cap returns coherent text.

rules: A timed cell counts only when the machine is quiet: load below 1.0 and no builds running.

B and C differ from A in their weights, so their outputs are not expected to match A; correctness for B, C and D is the pack census, coherent text, for B the paired MMLU accuracy gate against A, for C parity with B when the gate is unset, and for D agreement with C.
Speed is reported as change against A, per prompt size, cold and warm separately.
Failures and no-gain results are reported, not dropped.

execution.notes: Every model load runs under a 96 GiB cgroup cap with no swap, one heavy job at a time.

notes: Task graph written by hand as the demo starting point (no intake).
The seeded expert cache is the earlier change measured on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (engine.build_expert_weight_cache).
Revision 2 adds arm D and node size_prefill_batch after a probe on the Spark: arm B with -b 2048 -ub 2048 cut cold 2047-token TTFT from 311 s to 120 s with decode unchanged.
Revision 3 adds node measure_accuracy: the 2-bit pack must lose less than 5 MMLU points against the NVFP4 pack (paired, planned checkpoints, eval.paired_accuracy) before the lab.

Revision 4 (v3 file) makes every node contract preliminary: the scheduler agent finalizes each node just before it runs, binding capsules and filling slots from accepted upstream outputs, earlier failures and the machine state. A final contract may be more concrete or stricter than its preliminary one, never weaker.

Revision 5: the scheduler agent reported a spec gap on pin_inputs (2026-11-25): the free disk criterion asked for 1.4 TB, the room both packs need, while a run that reuses the packs writes almost nothing. The planner states it as free disk covering what the run writes plus 100 GB.

Revision 6 fills the device budget with expert cache (owner, 2026-11-26): the 2-bit arms take --moe-cache-mib from the size_prefill_batch plan (about 66 GiB instead of 60) under the same 110000 MiB device budget as arm A, whose NVFP4 compute buffer leaves it at 61440. Equal memory budget, not equal cache size, is the fair comparison; B against A then includes the cache room the smaller compute buffer frees.
Revision 6 also trims the lab protocol (owner, 2026-11-25): one warm request instead of two and 32 generated tokens instead of 128 per request, so the four arms fit in a few hours instead of a night.

Revision 6 (v4 file, owner decision 2026-11-25): a 2-bit pack not made before, routed experts IQ2_XXS for the gate and up projections, Q2_K for down, other tensors at their NVFP4-pack type (about 267 GB against 305 GB for the Q2_K pack of Nov 24), target iq2_xxs,down=q2_k for weights.build_weight_pack_compiler; and every node runs in this run (capped runs through factory.capped_runner), reusing nothing built by hand.

nodes.objective: Pin the stock llama.cpp tree, the official Muse NVFP4 checkpoint, the imatrix and the prompts by digest, and record the disk grant and memory cap.

outputs.name: pins
criteria: Names the stock commit 9048bad8 and the sha256 of every checkpoint shard, the index, the imatrix and each prompt.

Records free disk, the disk this run will write, the cgroup memory cap and the available memory before any load; free disk covers what the run writes plus 100 GB (about 0.9 TB when the NVFP4 and 2-bit packs are both written).
Records the checkpoint scale-plane layout per tensor role: packed weight, block scale, global scale_2, input scale.

slots.from: The capsule catalog, what the upstream nodes were built with and what failed before for this node.

nodes.objective: Extend the stock converter so it reads the stacked Muse NVFP4 experts and their scale planes, then write the NVFP4 GGUF pack.

outputs.name: converter
criteria: Splits experts.gate_up_proj into gate and up halves in the source order (gate first) and keeps NVFP4 blocks bit-for-bit (no dequantize and requantize).
Writes one [n_expert] .scale tensor per routed expert weight from weight_scale_2: gate takes column 0 and up column 1 of the [n_expert, 2] gate_up scale, down its [n_expert] scale.
Repacks lazily, one tensor at a time, and finishes under the 96 GiB memory cap (the stacked BF16 experts of the excluded layers 0 and 61 are the peak; 32 and 64 GiB caps were not enough).
Leaves the BF16 modules the checkpoint excludes (layers 0 and 61, self attention, lm_head) at their source type.
Times one expert before the full conversion and prints the projected total.
Touches only the files its capsule source map allows.

outputs.name: nvfp4_pack
criteria: Every routed expert weight in layers 1 to 60 is NVFP4 (ggml type 40) with a matching [n_expert] F32 .scale tensor.
The pack manifest lists per-file sha256, tensor census by type and total bytes.

slots.from: The capsule catalog, what the upstream nodes were built with and what failed before for this node.

nodes.objective: Apply the per-expert NVFP4 scale tensors in the Muse graph so the NVFP4 pack computes the same values as the checkpoint.

outputs.name: change
criteria: Passes the loaded ffn_gate_exps, ffn_up_exps and ffn_down_exps .scale tensors to the Muse mixture-of-experts block.
A pack without .scale tensors (the IQ2_XXS pack) gives byte-identical greedy output to stock.
One expert matmul and one layer slice of the NVFP4 pack match a torch dequantization of the checkpoint within the numerics tolerance.
Touches only the files its capsule source map allows.
With its switch unset (or the tensors it reads absent), the engine behaves exactly like stock: no new work, no changed output.
Errors and limits fall back to stock behaviour instead of crashing.

slots.from: The capsule catalog, what the upstream nodes were built with and what failed before for this node.

criteria: A source bundle of E0 against stock 9048bad8 with the sm_121 lab recipe, plus its build receipt.

outputs.name: smoke
criteria: One cold NVFP4 request under the 96 GiB cap returns coherent text; peak memory and available memory are recorded.

nodes.objective: Write a precision recipe and requantize the NVFP4 pack to a 2-bit pack: routed gate and up experts to IQ2_XXS and down experts to Q2_K (the down projection is the most sensitive to low bits), everything else kept at its source type.

outputs.name: recipe
criteria: Names the source pack digest, the target type per tensor role and the imatrix digest; every chosen type has a GB10 kernel.
Times one layer with the recipe's probe before the full run and records the projected full time; the full run starts only if it fits the node time limit.

outputs.name: pack_2bit
criteria: Every routed gate and up expert weight is IQ2_XXS and every down expert weight Q2_K; attention, norms, router, embeddings and output keep their NVFP4-pack type; .scale tensors carried unchanged.
Total size between 240 and 290 GB; the temporary disk peak stayed inside the grant.
Eight held-out prompts give coherent text; top-1 token agreement with the NVFP4 pack is reported, not claimed.

slots.from: The capsule catalog, what the upstream nodes were built with and what failed before for this node.
The census of the accepted NVFP4 pack and the disk grant: one criterion naming the expected 2-bit pack size.

nodes.objective: Measure how much accuracy the 2-bit pack loses against the NVFP4 pack on MMLU, paired question by question, and stop at the first planned checkpoint where the interval of the loss decides it against the margin.

outputs.name: accuracy
criteria: A muse-paired-accuracy/1 state: both arms scored on the same canonical zero-shot prompts, in the seeded order of the full MMLU test set, on real capped server loads of E0.
The paired interval of the loss acc(NVFP4) - acc(2-bit) at the first decisive planned checkpoint has its upper bound below 5 points.
